messages.body_plain:
I posted a solution to something similar to SO a while ago http://stackoverflow.com/questions/30474538/possible-to-show-console-messages-written-with-message-in-a-shiny-ui

In your case, something like this would work

printText <- function() {
  for(i in 1:10){
    Sys.sleep(0.1)

    shinyjs::html("text", paste("My text", i), add = TRUE)

    y = i + 1
  }
  return(y)
}

runApp(list(
  ui = shinyUI(fluidPage(
    shinyjs::useShinyjs(),

    titlePanel("Print consol output"),
    sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(actionButton("go", "Go")),
      mainPanel(

        div(id = "text")

      )
    )
  )),
  server = shinyServer(function(input, output, session){
    observeEvent(input$go, {

      shinyjs::html("text", "")

      y <- printText()
    })
  })
))

Basically, it's using the shinyjs package to manually change the HTML inside the element, instead of using shiny's reactivity.  If you can get Joe's solution to work, that'd be better though

messages.subject: Re: reactive expressions operating on an environment
messages.subject_clean: reactive expressions operating on an environment
messages.body_plain:
Absolutely do not do this. I'd try it with lists instead. Even though the lists are conceptually copied when passed between functions, my understanding is that R these days will actually share the underlying vectors in many cases, so very little additional memory will be consumed at each step (besides the new columns you're adding).

https://github.com/hadley/dplyr/issues/198

If you find otherwise, let me know.

> Hi, All:

> shinyServer(function(input, output) {
>
> readInData <- reactive({
>  retObj <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
>  retObj$dsRaw <- read.csv(inFile$datapath)
>  retObj
> })
>
> process1 <- reactive({
>  retObj <- readInData()
>  retObj$newObj <- ....
>
>  retObj
> })
>
> process2 <- reactive({
>   retObj <- process1()
>   retObj$var2 <- ....
>
>  retObj
> })
>
> #process 3, 4, 5 has the similar style
> }
>
> And different renderX() functions will call process1() or process2(),... to get their necessary data. My reactive data steps pass along one enviroment that contains everything, and all they do is to modify variables in the environment. Is this a good approach? I heard recently that using the side effect of functions is not recommended.

It's really hard for me to say without a reproducible case. That said, UTF-16 is quite surprising--I personally almost never see that encoding (the closest I have seen in UCS-2 on Windows). This is a stab in the dark but maybe the default endian-ness is swapped on Linux vs. Mac? Are UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE valid encodings on Mac and/or Linux?

On Thu, Mar 31, 2016 at 1:03 PM Ed Lee <edy...@google.com> wrote:
> Hi Joe - I wanted to follow up on my response. Please let me know if you have any suggestions. Thanks!
>
> On Wed, Mar 30, 2016 at 12:10 PM Ed Lee <edy...@google.com> wrote:
> > Hi Joe -
> >
> > Code in question: read.csv(inFile2$datapath, sep="\t", fileEncoding="UTF-16", stringsAsFactors = F)
> >
> > The reason why out$assessment and output$summary are showing errors in the log (yet also showing errors in the load bar) is probably because I have an input$run condition upon loading my input csv; and I do all of my data transformation in the reactive object before it gets to output$. There are two errors I see when running the analysis on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> server:
> >
> > Error: object 'bid.modifier' not found
> > Error: argument "subset" is missing, with no default
> >
> > But I tried running this in linux environment, and I get the following message:
> >
> > Warning in scan(file, what, nmax, sep, dec, quote, skip, nlines, na.strings, : invalid input found on input connection
> >
> > As I mentioned before, this loads and runs fine on my local MAC.
> >
> > Based on this, I'm coming to the conclusion that there may be unusual characters (i.e. ®, #, etc.) not encoded in UTF-16 csv file that breaks my read.csv code, and MACs are more robust in handling these. With that said, here are my follow up questions:
> > what approach do I have to avoid this situation on shiny where users are inputting their own downloaded csv with potentially unforeseen, unusual characters?
> > if this has more to do with what fileEncoding I'm using in read.csv, what way do I have to identify the best fileEncoding to use? I have used UTF-16 for this dataset for other cids and have worked fine so I've just assumed this is the fileEncoding for this data set.

messages.subject: hover functionality for multiple plot: coordinates not retrieved at the extreme side of the plot
messages.subject_clean: hover functionality for multiple plot: coordinates not retrieved at the extreme side of the plot
messages.body_plain:
I have a multiple plot in base R created with par(mfrow = c(...)), and would like to retrieve the coordinates of the hover.
The hover coordinates are correctly displayed, but not retrieved for the sides of the plot (on which the multiple plot is used).

Here is an example for a two-columns layout:

library(shiny)
# server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

    output$testPlot <- renderPlot({
        par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
        plot(1:10, 1:10, main = "Plot 1")
        plot(1:10, 1:10, main = "Plot 2")
    })

    output$testPlotHooverCoordinates <- renderText({
        paste0("hoover coordinates: x = ", input$testPlotHoover$x, "\ny = ",
            input$testPlotHoover$y)
    })

})

# ui.R
shinyUI(
    fluidPage(
        textOutput("testPlotHooverCoordinates"),
        plotOutput(outputId = "testPlot",
            hover = hoverOpts(
            id = "testPlotHoover",
            delay = 10
        ))
    )
)

 [5] Rcpp_0.12.3     jsonlite_0.9.19 digest_0.6.9    xtable_1.8-2

The coordinates are not retrieved at the left side of the left plot, and at the right side of the right plot.

Note: I am sure there are better way to create such interactive plots in shiny, but I would like to use the R base implementation of the underline function (more complex than the example), which is implemented with par(mfrow()) .

Is this a known/expected issue?

I currently serve internal apps for my group using the open source version of shiny server. My only complaint at this point is the speed of my apps. Would using nginx or similar improve speed, security, and/or functionality? I know proxying will allow things like authentication and secure connections to be set up, but I'm primarily interested in speeding things up.

thanks,

-Brett

messages.subject: Re: why use nginx?
messages.subject_clean: why use nginx?
messages.body_plain:
nginx will not speed up how fast a shiny app runs.

nginx in this case really just acts as a router, moving requests to a certain URI to your app.  after nginx hands off the request, its all up to shiny-server, and nginx cannot speed that up.

messages.subject: Re: why use nginx?
messages.subject_clean: why use nginx?
messages.body_plain:
If you solely needed your server to run shiny then the shiny-server front-end should do.

However, when integrating shiny apps with other web sites then nginx is useful.  For example, if you have nginx serving a web site on standard port 80, www.site.com <http://www.site.com>.  You might want your shiny app at www.site.com/shinyapp <http://www.site.com/shinyapp>.

With nginx you can easily set your server block config for www.site.com <http://www.site.com> to have something like

location /shinyapp {
  proxy_pass localhost:3838/shinyapp;
}

In short, shiny server does fine serving an app from a single location, but when you need more flexibility in integrating an app into other services, nginx's location blocks and proxy functions make this task routine.

Erik

messages.subject_clean: tabsets: position on the left
messages.body_plain:
Yes, this is unfortunate. Bootstrap 3 has removed the ability to position tabs anywhere but "above" (a lot of other people have complained about this <https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/issues/8922>). See this stackoverflow post <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/18432577/stacked-tabs-in-bootstrap-3> for ideas of getting around this using css. Because of this, we're about to deprecate the `position` argument to `tabsetPanel()` in Shiny. Sorry :(

messages.body_plain:
Hi Carsten,

Thanks for including your code with your question. It looks like you have several misconceptions here. You generally never want to:

* Assign an output from inside of an observer (well, not NEVER never, but you certainly don't want to in this case)
* Declare an eventReactive or reactive from inside of a render function

Generally, observe(), observeEvent(), eventReactive, reactive, and assignments to outputs should all be performed at the top level of the server function. I can see what you're trying to do here, but it's based on an incorrect mental model of reactive programming. Fortunately, this is the exact mental model I try to counteract in this talk: https://www.rstudio.com/resources/videos/effective-reactive-programming/ It's two hours, or a little more if you follow along with the materials and do the exercises (which I highly recommend), but it will save you many hours of frustration in the future as you start using Shiny's reactive primitives as they were intended to be used.

messages.subject: ggplot2 with custom stat works on cmd but not in shiny, error : "No stat called StatStepribbon"
messages.subject_clean: ggplot2 with custom stat works on cmd but not in shiny, error : "No stat called StatStepribbon"
messages.body_plain:
I created shinyApp which plots the survival data using the ggplot2. I wanted to plot the confidence interval as a filled polygon using the geom_ribbon. Unfortunately the provided geom_ribbon does not support "step-like" polygon.
For that I used the code from ggplot2 mailing list (https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/ggplot2/9cFWHaH1CPs <https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#%21topic/ggplot2/9cFWHaH1CPs>) which works fine on the command line.
However when using it in the shinyApp, it does not produce the plot and instead it gives an error : "No stat called StatStepribbon.".

The only way how to get it to work is to save the functions into a separate file and load it with:

source("functions.R", local=FALSE)

which loads it into global environment. Only then ggplot2 can find the defined stat. It does not work when functions are created in local shiny environment. The code is available here:

https://gist.github.com/ivanek/d480c0c853ea79eab82d6ef8bac9363a

I would appreciate your help.
Best
Robert

Hi Sanjana,

at the moment I didn't find a good solution, so I just applied a trick that I don't like but it works.
So I copied the r function code directly inside the server.r file, so that now the r functions are loaded directly inside it.
Maybe this is not the correct way (my server.r file has know more than 3000 rows...), and I cannot says if the loading can take a little extra-time with this solution.
I think that the correct way should be to create, test and develop an r package containing your function/s, then distribute and publish it on the Cran or the GitHub using devtools. So in this way you will load your function just loading the package, using library("...") in the server.r file, but this work requires time.
Let me know if you find a smarter way to do it :)

Thank you!!!

Hi Mark, the code in linkedScatter itself is correct; but when calling callModule, you want to pass the reactive itself by name (car_data) without reading it (car_data()).

callModule(linkedScatter, "scatters", car_data)

This is similar to how you can pass a function by name to something like lapply:

lapply(letters, toupper) # works
lapply(letters, toupper()) # doesn't work

I host the website internally by running runApp(file = <file name>, host = "<Server IP address>", port = <port no.>) on R studio. I'm not sure how the back end works in R shiny in order to split into three tiers.

Thank you.

messages.subject: Re: R Shiny Hosting on 3 Tier Server Architecture
messages.subject_clean: R Shiny Hosting on 3 Tier Server Architecture
messages.body_plain:
This shouldn't be too complicated. I'd do it this way:

1.  Set up database server.  Make sure port is open to be accessed by local network. E.g,. using MySQL, port 3306 should be opened.
2.  Test connecting to database from app machine.
3.  Install R and shiny server open source on the APP machine.  Install the shiny app in /srv/shiny-server/app.  Make sure the DBI objects have the new DB server IP as the host (default is localhost or 127.0.0.1).  Yes, it's called shiny server, but here it's just acting as an interface between R/Shiny and the web server.
4.  Make sure the shiny server port (usually 3838) is open on the app machine.
5.  Set up web server.  Install nginx.  Create a server block proxying web requests to the shiny app server.

That's the basic idea.  Very straightforward.

Erik

messages.subject: Re: timeout setting, or a remedy for a long loading time
messages.subject_clean: timeout setting, or a remedy for a long loading time
messages.body_plain:
Your timeout is mostly likely a network connection timeout. When you set app_init_timeout, that controls the response time from R process and used for situations that your application does a lot of computations before it completely loads. But in your case that doesn't seem to be the issue since you can start it up in your office pretty quickly. You might want to check your VPN settings.

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Joe. I think I implemented the two modifications you suggested, but the code crashes:

# Module
# Module UI function
csvFileInput <- function(id, label = "CSV file") {
  # Create a namespace function using the provided id
  ns <- NS(id)
  tagList(
    checkboxInput(ns("agree"), p("I read ",
                                 a("the very important stuff",
                                   href="http://stackoverflow.com/",
                                   target="_blank"))),
    fileInput(ns("file"), label)
  )
}

# Module server function
csvFile <- function(input, output, session) {
  # The selected file, if any
  userFile <- reactive({
    # If no file is selected, don't do anything
    validate(need(input$file, message = FALSE))
    input$file
  })
  # The user's data, parsed into a data frame
  dataframe <- reactive({
    readr::read_csv(userFile()$datapath)
  })
  # We can run observers in here if we want to
  observe({
    msg <- sprintf("File %s was uploaded", userFile()$name)
    cat(msg, "\n")
  })
  # Return the reactive that yields the data frame
  return(dataframe)
}

diable_button <- function(input, output, session, button, agree){
  observe({

    if (agree() == T) {

      # enable the download button
      shinyjs::enable(button)
    }
  })

  observe({

    if (agree() == F) {

      # enable the download button
      shinyjs::disable(button)
    }
  })
}

## app.R ##
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)
library(shinyjs)
# Header
header <- dashboardHeader()
# Sidebar
sidebar <- dashboardSidebar(
  csvFileInput("datafile", "CSV file")
)
# Body

  useShinyjs(),
  box(
    title = "Test",
    width = 12,
    solidHeader = TRUE,
    status = "warning",
    dataTableOutput("table")
  )
)
# ui
ui <- dashboardPage(header, sidebar, body)
# server
server <- function(input, output) {
  datafile <- callModule(csvFile, "datafile")

  callModule(diable_button, "datafile",
             button = input$chosenfile,

             agree = reactive(input$agree))

  output$table <- renderDataTable({
    datafile()
  })

}
#run
shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.subject: Update numeric input with click?
messages.subject_clean: Update numeric input with click?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Everyone,

I have and app that generates a plot that is a function of a numeric input. I would like to add the option of updating the numeric input (and therefore the plot) by clicking on the graph.

This is the code I wrote:

set.seed(4132)
df.plot <- data.frame(density=rnorm(100))

## app.R ##
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)
# Header
header <- dashboardHeader()
# Sidebar
sidebar <- dashboardSidebar(numericInput(
  "cutoff",
  label = h4("Cutoff:"),
  value = 0,
  step = 0.01
))
# Body
body <- dashboardBody(
  plotOutput("plot", click = "plot_click"),
  verbatimTextOutput("info")
)
# ui
ui <- dashboardPage(header, sidebar, body)
# server
server <- function(input, output) {
  ds.data <- reactive({
    ds <- density(df.plot$density,
                  from = min(df.plot$density),
                  to = input$cutoff)
    ds_data <- data.frame(x = ds$x, y = ds$y)
    return(ds_data)
  })

  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(df.plot, aes(density)) + geom_density() +
      geom_vline(xintercept = input$cutoff) +
      geom_area(data = ds.data(), aes(x = x, y = y))
  })

  output$info <- renderText({
    paste0("x=", input$plot_click$x, "\n",
           "y=", input$plot_click$y)
  })

  observe({
    updateNumericInput("cutoff", value = input$plot_click$y)
  })

}
#run
shinyApp(ui, server)

Alas, it gives me this error:

Listening on http://127.0.0.1:4668
Warning: Error in $: $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors
Stack trace (innermost first):
    58: updateNumericInput
    57: observerFunc [#22]
     4: <Anonymous>
     3: do.call
     2: print.shiny.appobj
     1: <Promise>
ERROR: [on_request_read] connection reset by peer

If I take out the observe, the code works but it does not update the input...

Thanks for the help!

Ignacio

messages.subject: Storing text input into a variable conditional on a selection from drawdown window
messages.subject_clean: Storing text input into a variable conditional on a selection from drawdown window
messages.body_plain:
Hi guys,

I have the following problem (and for quite some time I am not able to solve it). I am trying to store a text input corresponding to e.g. "option 1" from a drop-down into a variable (in userEnv). Next, I want to change the selection in the drop-down, to e.g. "option 2" and again retrieve the text to a variable and store, etc.

I am attaching my codes for server.R and ui.R below.

Can anyone advise me, please, on what should I do in order to keep the text input saved in the userEnv, even after I choose another to option. Also, I would like to be able to review my inputs after being typed in.

Thx a bunch!

A) server.R:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  userEnv <- new.env()
  userEnv$text <- NULL

  optionID <- reactive({
    isolate({print("inside reactive")})
    if(is.null(input$SELoption)){return(NULL)}
    return(input$SELoption)
  })

  observe({
    fID <- optionID()

    isolate({print("inside observe")})
    isolate({print(paste0("fID: ", fID))})

    if(!is.null(userEnv$text[[fID]])) updateTextInput(session, "text", value = userEnv$text[[fID]])
    isolate({print(paste0("input$text: ", input$text))})

  })

})

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
B) ui.R:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(shiny)

shinyUI(fluidPage(

  sidebarPanel(
    selectInput('SELoption', label = "Select option",
                choices = c(
                  "Option 1" = 'f1',
                  "Option 2" = 'f2',
                  "Option 3" = 'f3'),
                selected = 'f1')
  ),

  mainPanel(
    textInput("text", label = strong("Text"), value = 0)
  )
))
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

messages.subject: Modifying Filter and Pagination behaviour in RShiny Datatable
messages.subject_clean: Modifying Filter and Pagination behaviour in RShiny Datatable
messages.body_plain:
I have a few tables (10-15) that are several million rows long. I'd like to expose them via the DT feature in RShiny with the ability to filter in real-time. However, because it can take a long time to filter a table that is sufficiently large, I'd like to use my own function that can be applied on the filters to retrieve the results (rather than having datatable process the same).

1) Using a custom filter function

As a simple example, if the data was coming from a sql table, t as follows:

a b c 1 2 3 4 5 6 1 2 3

And if I had to find all values of a == 1, I can either use the DataTable filter or instead send a query back - eg., select * from t where a==1. Similarly, select * from t where a==1, b==2, ... etc. The latter method (select from ...) is what I'd like to use. I am using an HPC Timeseries database that could process these queries much faster than using the in-built functionality.

2) I'd also like to be able to interact with the page number so that I retrieve only those rows that are required for the current display. Taking the above table, t as an example, if the user was on page 1, I'd only retrieve the first x rows (eg., 10 rows is Show 10 Entries were selected) and when the user clicks on Page 2, I'd retrieve the next set of 10 rows.

There is a slight caveat in that the pagination happens automatically, but I'd be able to provide the count of rows such that the pagination can be accurate (eg., based on the user filter criteria the count of the table is x rows, and hence show x/10 pagination buttons)

I am not sure if this can be done - whether via datatable or through any other means. Would be grateful if someone could advise further on this. Thanks, Raj.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

my apologies for not being precise enough, let me try to rephrase. I am trying to achieve the following functionality:

On the side-bar panel I want to have the drop-down with 3 options to choose ("option 1", "option 2", "option 3"). The main panel should be a conditional panel, where the condition is linked to the drop-down, each of the panel containing a textInput. In this simplified example, however, I abstract from the conditional panel, and have only a single textInput window (since this is the hurdle I am not able to pass). Now, what I would like to be able to do is to:

1) have a default value of "0" in the text input
2) choose "option 1" and fill for example "a" instead of "0" in the textInput box. Store this "a" to userEnv$text[["option 1"]]
3) choose "option 2" and fill for example "b" instead of "0" in the textInput box. Store this "b" to userEnv$text[["option 2"]]
4) choose "option 3" and fill for example "c" instead of "0" in the textInput box. Store this "c" to userEnv$text[["option 3"]]
5) choose "option 1" again. Now, I would like to see "a" already in the text input, since this has been filled in before. So basically the text input will now update based on userEnv$text[["option 1"]].

General remarks:
- I am trying to achieve persistence with this userEnv variable, so after I restart the app, I will not have to fill-in all the textInputs again, rather those that has been filled previously will be loaded from the userEvn.

Is my point clearer now?

Hello, me again, working my way through  Shiny modules :)

I have cross-posted to SO here: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/36841477/shiny-modules-how-to-access-the-input-of-a-looped-shiny-module

I'm trying to make a helper function that will filter/aggregate any data.frame.  I am as far as getting some dynamic selectInputs which is already useful, but I now want to put those selectInputs into a loop within server.R so I can subset a data.frame by their selected values.

The problem seems to be that the inputs that are generated within the Shiny server loop can not be accessed via normal Shiny modules means, and the syntax for finding their names eludes me.  The issue lies within these lines:

      new_data <- reactive({

          str(i) ## debug to check its in loop

          agg <- aggs[i]

          ## How to access the dynamic_select inputs selected?
          inputA <- input[[agg]]  # is NULL?
          old_col <- old_data[[agg]] # is NULL?

          str(inputA) ## debug - NULL should hold values of dynamic inputs

          new_data <- old_data[inputA %in% old_col,]

          old_data <- new_data

        }

        new_data

      })

Does anyone have an idea on how to access the selected values that should be appearing in variable inputA ?

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Modules: how to access the input$ of a looped Shiny Module?
messages.subject_clean: Shiny Modules: how to access the input$ of a looped Shiny Module?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark,

I don't understand the overall aim of the app, but I'll tell you the answer to your specific question and hopefully that will help.

The general rule for modules is that you can only access the value of a moduleUI's input, in the corresponding module server function. In this case, you can only access the value of dynamicSelectInput from within dynamicSelect. If you want to then make that value available to other modules, then you have to return it as a reactive from the module server function. In this case, that means that the dynamicSelect function should end with this line:

  return(reactive(input$dynamic_select))

("return" is optional but I think it helps make explicit the fact that reactive(input$dynamic_select) is the return value.)

Then, in outerTable, you could do something like this instead of your for-loop:

  selectResults <- lapply(setNames(aggs, aggs), function(agg) {
    callModule(module = dynamicSelect,
      id = agg,
      the_data = the_data,
      column = agg)
  })

Now selectResults is a named list, each element being a reactive expression (so selectResults[[agg]]() to retrieve a value).

That said, I made those changes to your code but could not figure out what the relationship between old_data, new_data, and the_data is supposed to be, so I can't provide you with a working example.

Hi again,

I am slowly getting back to this topic, with some more results this time.
I managed to get some results, but there are still things I don't completely understand. Here is the current workflow:

- click in the "console", which creates a textarea
- the textarea has a "blur" event, and if the key pressed is "Enter" it stores the text into a local object (say Rcommand)
- I'm using:

Shiny.onInputChange("Rcommand", Rcommand);

to trigger the server side, and I have previously specified:

Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler("Rcommand",
    function(object) {
        outres = object;
    }
);

(to store the response in the object outres)

On the server.R file, I have:

observe({
    foo <- input$Rcommand
    textoutput <- capture.output(tryCatch(eval(parse(text = foo)), error = function(e) e))
    session$sendCustomMessage(type = "Rcommand", list(textoutput))
})

(for the moment I am just testing things with eval() and parse() before using the evaluate package).

> ls()
[1] "foo"

So the object test is not stored, and not listed by ls().
I am probably lost in the environments wilderness. What I would like is to evaluate the command from the webpage, in the environment of the server.R file.

Adrian

The chart is an html widget created from a JS library using htmlwidgets package.  Currently every change to the chart requires me to build the chart once again which is time consuming and not user friendly.  The chart.validateNow() method in the JS library allows us to plot the chart post changes made to it without having to render and build it again from scratch every time some property within it is changed (be it the graphs or title or color etc.).

The creator of the package is not clear how to implement the chart.validateNow() method but my hunch is that if it can be done in JS it should be doable within R.  Appreciate your views.

messages.body_plain:
Stated a bit more clearly:
Can session$clientData$url_search change without starting a new Shiny *session*?

(If not, then why is it a reactive variable?)

On Tuesday, April 26, 2016 at 1:17:02 AM UTC-4, Joel M. wrote:
> It seems like in all the situations I've found in which session$clientData$url_search changes (such as by modifying the part of the URL after the "?" in the browser or by clicking on a link to the same Shiny app, but a different url_search), the entire Shiny app is re-executed.  Are there any situations in which url_search changes without the Shiny app being re-started?  In other words, are there ways to have url_search change, and then only those reactives that are dependent on url_search are executed, without restarting the whole app from scratch?

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have the following problem:

I created a function that, given certain certain parameters, creates/updates plots in a Shiny Application.

This function is called from within an observer.

My problem here is that I cannot assign the plots from the function directly to the output object, as assign() won't work to access list items and <<- tells me that it cannot find output object. On top of that, I cannot get the output object inside the function, modify it and return it back because shiny won't let you access output objects.

However, if I assign it with <<- inside an observer, it works fine but is not what I need.

The example below:

The function would be something like:

updatePlots <- function(data,var){

output[["plot1"]] <- renderPlot(hist(data[[var]]))
}

and is called in an observer with a reactive dataset like this one

observe(updatePlots(shiny.dataset(),input$selected.var))

This works

observe({

output[["plot1"]] <<- renderPlot(hist(shiny.dataset(),input$selected.var))

Thank you!

library(shiny)
library(DT)
library(sqldf)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  mtcars$carName <- rownames(mtcars)

  output$carList <- DT::renderDataTable({
    searchStr <- input$car

    if (searchStr != "")  sqldf(paste0("select * from mtcars where carName like '%",searchStr,"%'"))
  }, selection = 'single', rownames = F)

  output$testOutput = renderPrint(input$carList_rows_selected)

messages.subject: Re: numericInput comma separator with jQuery

messages.body_plain:
Hi Josh,

I'm sorry it took us so long to get back to you. Here <https://beta.rstudioconnect.com/barbara/format-numbers/> is an app (you can find the full repo in my Github account <https://github.com/bborgesr/format_numbers>) that gives you two options (and I think the second one is really what you want). The advantage to the first one is that you don't need any Javascript and you don't have to remember to coerce your value back into a comma-less numeric type. Please note that this is not really an "official" solution and you do lose some functionality, as explained in the app. We're hoping to actually give this option as an argument to the numericInput() function in the future. messages.subject: Re: htmlTemplate not reflecting changes on page refresh
messages.subject_clean: htmlTemplate not reflecting changes on page refresh
messages.body_plain:
Ah, good point. There are two things you could do:

1) Wrap your UI definition with function(req) { ... }. So for example, if you have this:

# ui.R
htmlTemplate(...)

Instead you would replace it with:

# ui.R
function(req) {
  htmlTemplate(...)
}

This will prevent the caching from happening. Oh, if you're using the (vestigial) shinyUI function then it would look like:

shinyUI(function(req) {
  htmlTemplate(...)
})

2) Leave things the way they are, but before launching, call options(shiny.autoreload=TRUE). I believe this should make it so saving your HTML template will immediately cause the app to reload, no need to even refresh your browser (unless there's an error in your template, then you'll still need to manually reload).

You need to use a reactive expression--this is the core of what Shiny reactive programming is about. You can see a simple example here:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/tree/master/inst/examples/03_reactivity

This example happens to use textual and tabular output, but you'd do the same thing in your case but just have a plotOutput instead of verbatimTextOutput/tableOutput.

I also highly recommend watching the videos on Effective Reactive Programming here:
https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/

Hope that helps!

df <- data.frame(x=1:6, z=7:12, y=c("A", "B","C", "D", "E", "F"))

# Define UI for application that draws a histogram
ui <- (fluidPage(

  # Application title
  titlePanel("Select Inputs"),

  # Sidebar with a slider input for number of bins
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("groups", "Pick groups", c("A", "B", "C"),
                  selectize=FALSE, multiple = TRUE),
      selectInput("groups2", "Pick groups", c("D", "E", "F"),
                  selectize=FALSE, multiple = TRUE)

      ##would like to add a button here that would reset plot on click

    ),

    # Show a plot of the generated distribution
    mainPanel(
      #tableOutput('table'),
      highchartOutput("hcontainer",height = "500px")#,

    )
  )
))

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram
server <- shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  firstsub <- reactive({
    subset(df, df$y %in% input$groups)
  })

  secondsub <- reactive({
    subset(df, df$y %in% input$groups2)
  })

  thirdsub <- reactive({
    rbind(firstsub(), secondsub())
  })

  #output$table <- renderTable(thirdsub())
  output$hcontainer <- renderHighchart({

    unique.tmp <- unique(thirdsub()$y)

    TEST1 <- highchart()

    for(i in 1:length(unique.tmp)){
      tmp <- subset(thirdsub(), thirdsub()$y==unique.tmp[i])

      TEST <- list.parse2(tmp[,1:2])

      TEST1 <-TEST1 %>%
        hc_add_serie(name=unique.tmp[i], type="scatter", data=TEST)
    }

    TEST1
  })

})

# Run the application
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

      m_rent<-addTiles(m_rent)
      pal<-colorNumeric("Reds", c(50,400),na.color="transparent")
      m_rent<-addRasterImage(m_rent,raster_nb_rent2, colors = pal, opacity = 0.5)

      m_rent<-addLegend(m_rent,position="topleft",pal,values=values(raster_nb_rent2),title=cat("estimation"))

     })
